findings.reason: without a stated criterion for an acceptable reason (the sibling §5 says "the source-domain reason its members differ"), the node can close on a graph it did not change.
findings.text: the first bullet reads "zero families whose members carry more than one `physics_domain`, or lists each remaining family with the recorded reason it stands": the second branch has no criterion for the reason, so a pass that changes no name and writes a reason on every divergent family satisfies it, and only the eight §1 families are pinned to a single domain

findings.reason: the one accuracy bar in the plan measures the case that was never broken.
findings.text: the per-family decision's accuracy is to be compared against the per-name decision's "on the labelled names the domain decision was calibrated on in `sn-catalog-grouping`", a set that files 73 calibration rows into ~70 families (3 groups hold more than one row, and the one group with differing labels — `poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field` with `breakdown_magnetic_field` — is not a family at all): on near-singleton families the per-family decision is the per-name decision, so "not lower" holds however badly the method behaves on the split families the plan exists for

findings.reason: a done section whose measurement has no durable path leaves the next reader to re-derive it before trusting any of the plan.
findings.text: §1 is the plan's whole evidence base (the eight-family table, transport holding 698 of 1,975, 8 of 20 species families split) and cites no artifact; a search of `docs/` for `X_density_at_pedestal_top` returns only this plan, so the census behind the root cause cannot be opened or re-run

findings.reason: a one-sided handoff leaves §5's builder re-doing §3's work or closing §5 on §3's evidence, and neither plan records which.
findings.text: §3 states "This absorbs the grouping half of `sn-catalog-consistency` §5: that section keeps its domain-audit endpoint, and its family-agreement endpoint is met here", but this plan declares no `informs`, `gates` or `depends-on` link to that plan, and §5 still says "This section also owns grouping across each family" with its own census done-when intact

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `sn-catalog-consistency` §1 and §5 carry the quoted counts and the domain-audit endpoint; the calibration label set resolves at `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-catalog-grouping/scg-domain-label-sheet.json` with 73 calibration of 150 rows; the one-writer guard resolves to a package-wide static scan, which is why "passing unchanged" is a meaningful claim for a new in-package write site; the domain audit exists at `imas_codex/standard_names/domain_audit.py`. The gate directory `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-per-family/` is a destination the node creates, not a citation.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's read-back passes on "each remaining family with the recorded reason it stands", an escape with no criterion, and §2's accuracy comparison is run on a labelled set that is almost entirely one name per family, so "not lower" cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §1's census table and the 698-of-1,975 and 98-of-125 counts cite no artifact; the only place `X_density_at_pedestal_top` appears is the plan text itself.
rubric_items.naming: pass — section ids are structure, and the plan-named evidence directory is the repo's house convention for every peer plan; the only version string is the catalog release the measurement is taken on.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence and the code: a name is offered only its own source paths' and IDSs' domains, the band umbrellas and `general` (`imas_codex/standard_names/domain_decision.py:6-8,134-148`), a single candidate is taken with no call (line 258), and `export.py` carries no family/domain agreement check, so "the export does not check it" holds. Each section states records and tolerances rather than a code path.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 delivers one domain decision per family, §3 brings the live families to it, §4 makes a cut refuse a split family; each node's bullets serve its one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §3 declares it absorbs the family-agreement endpoint of `sn-catalog-consistency` §5, but no relationship is declared to that plan and §5 still declares the same endpoint as its own done-when.
